title: pl blend
parentNote: pl finishes the set of l blends: bl, cl and now pl. The slip to listen for is a little vowel sneaking into the middle, so plum comes out "puh-lum" — say the p and the l on their own, slowly, then run them together with nothing between them at all. The other wobble is plan and pan, which sound nearly the same to a child who is guessing from the first letter, and there is a listening activity today that asks for exactly that pair. Four days of new beginnings in a row is a lot; if they are flagging, do the story and leave the review until tomorrow.

activities.mouthCue: Pop your lips shut for the p, then flick your tongue up behind your teeth for the l.
activities.prompt: Two letters, two sounds, said in a hurry. No little vowel in the middle.
All three end with an l. Which one starts with a pop at your lips?
Two of these are one sound on its own. Find the pair.
The new blend goes first. Slide the two sounds together before you say the rest.
Now keep pl in one piece. Three sounds: pl, o, t.
Four sounds. Do not let the t slip off the end.
A blend on the front and a blend on the back.
One of these has an extra sound at the front. Listen before the vowel.
All three start the same. The last sound decides it.
Same again. The word is longer than it sounds.

activities.text: The plum fell off and did plop in the pond.
Dan dug a plot and did plant a plum pit in it.
Meg did plug in the lamp and the shed lit up.

activities.title: The plum plan
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Meg and Dan had a plan. They did plant a plum pit in a plot.
A plump duck did plod up the hill and sat on the plot!
Meg did clap and clap and the plump duck did plod off.
Dan set a plank up on the plot and the duck did not get back in.
In the end a plum plant did pop up. The plan did not flop!
